properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. From the xrt-demo genesis report (F4, F5, F7, N3) and bhome Session 2 (the skew table), 2026-09-16.

═══ THE FIVE, with the cheapest answer beside each ═══
(1) ⭐ F5 — the genesis skill: "if the brief already states the structure concretely, capture it and let DETECT check it, rather than withholding what they wrote." One sentence; the reporter followed the rule, withheld five elements with positions in metres, and flagged it. The rule's reasoning (fire concept_without_design so structure is answered WITH the user) is right for a vague brief and wrong for a specific one. Cheapest of the five and the only one with no design question in it.
(2) F4 — describe_schema: `required_only` is useless for "does Artifact declare status?" and the full read is 24,005 characters of edge catalogue. A `fields: required | all | none` three-way, or `properties_only`. Cheap; the budget machinery already exists.
(3) F7 — schema-loading cost: ~20 ToolSearch fetches across four rounds before the first write, because the harness defers ~200 tools. Partly the harness's. But add_design_rule's `steps` already validates against served skill and tool names, so get_skill could return the tools a skill names — a `tools` list per skill, derived, not maintained.
(4) N3 — unrealized_capability at genesis: 14 of 21 findings one per capability where nothing is built; the phase gaps already say it once. A rollup when EVERY capability is unrealized (the design has not started building) would read more honestly than enumeration — the aggregate/per-node question cap:aggregate-gap-keying holds, applied to the empty-build case. ⚠️ Counter: per-capability keying is what lets one acknowledgement not silence the next capability; the rollup must be keyed on "nothing built yet" and dissolve into per-node findings the moment one is.
(5) VERSION SKEW (bhome, nine calls): errors arrive one field at a time — add_decision cost three round trips for one logical call — and the skew is silent until the first failure. The RequiredFields helper already lists every required field at once; unknown-field errors come from serde one at a time. A handshake notice in get_instructions ("your client's tool list is N versions behind; reconnect") would turn nine failures into one warning; the server knows its version and the client's connection time. Precedent: fact:defect-a-clients-tool-list-is-fixed-at-connection (2026-09-06) — known, and the field cost is now measured at nine per session.

═══ WHAT IS NOT HERE ═══
The two worst findings of the same report — add_artifact writing `realized`, and the guard refusing thread pairs — are root-caused separately (fact:root-cause-add-artifact-…, fact:root-cause-the-guard-still-refuses-thread-pairs-…) because they are defects with causes, not ergonomics.
properties.name: OPEN — five genesis frictions from one run: the skill's bolded "do NOT create Components yet" has no clause for a brief that already states the structure; describe_schema cannot answer "does this type have field X?" in under 24 KB; ~20 tool schemas were fetched before the first write and get_skill could name the tools a skill needs; 14 of 21 findings were unrealized_capability on a project where nothing is built; and nine calls failed on version skew one field at a time with no warning at handshake
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill from two field reports, nothing promoted. Five items in one node because each is a genesis-round cost with a one-line cheapest answer, and a person deciding "which of these do we do" wants them side by side; the two defects were kept out so this node cannot be half-answered by fixing them.
